findings.source_passage: so do their diligent tracings-out not belie the obvious deduction. To trail the genealogies of these high mortal miseries, carries us at last among the sourceless primogenitures of the gods
findings.why_it_matters: The draft omits 'so do their diligent tracings-out not belie the obvious deduction' entirely and runs the 'trail the genealogies' clause directly without the connective logic, losing the rhetorical pivot that makes the philosophical argument cohere and gives it its distinctive Melvillean stride.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'so do their diligent tracings-out not belie the obvious deduction' before the 'to trail the genealogies' clause to preserve the full rhetorical shape of the philosophical digression.

findings.source_passage: that ever-contracting, dropping circle ashore, who, for any reason, possessed the privilege of a less banned approach to him
findings.why_it_matters: The draft compresses to 'that ever-contracting, timid circle ashore who possessed the privilege of approach,' losing 'dropping,' 'for any reason,' 'a less banned approach to him' — the word 'banned' especially carries interpretive weight about Ahab's self-imposed exile and the aura of prohibition around him.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'dropping,' 'for any reason,' and 'a less banned approach to him' in the circle-ashore phrase to preserve the characterization of Ahab's inaccessibility.

findings.source_passage: not only this, but to that ever-contracting, dropping circle ashore…invested itself with terrors…So that, through their zeal for him, they had all conspired, so far as in them lay, to muffle up the knowledge
findings.why_it_matters: The draft collapses 'they had all conspired, so far as in them lay, to muffle up the knowledge of this thing from others' into passive construction ('was muffled from others'), erasing the conspiratorial agency of the crew/circle ashore, which is an interpretive nuance about the social suppression of Ahab's wound.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore active construction: 'they had all conspired, so far as in them lay, to muffle up the knowledge of this thing from others' to preserve the sense of collective complicity.

summary: The draft preserves all major signatures faithfully, including the full philosophical digression on Grief and Joy, the 'gods themselves are not for ever glad' line, and the 'ineffaceable, sad birth-mark' close; minor flattening occurs in one rhetorical pivot and in the description of the 'banned' circle ashore, but no high-severity failures are present.
